export_controls.text:
We’re seeing the risks of the AI race unfold in real time. Selling advanced AI chips to China would make those risks worse.  

I’m joining 14 of my colleagues in urging President Trump: Do not sell advanced American AI chips to the Chinese government. https://t.co/mHjYv1Is7r

deepseek.reason: The speaker urges President Trump not to sell advanced American AI chips to the Chinese government.
deepseek.confidence_reason: The statement directly calls for restricting advanced AI chip sales to China.

export_controls.text:
China just launched the first ever AI-powered cyber attack against the U.S.

And Donald Trump just announced a deal to sell China the most advanced chips that power AI.
 
I asked four leading cybersecurity experts if they think this is a good idea. Spoiler alert: they don’t. https://t.co/Ji3KoYUNpo

deepseek.reason: He criticizes the advanced chip sale to China and cites cybersecurity experts opposing it.
deepseek.confidence_reason: The speaker's opposition is implied through rhetorical framing and expert citation rather than a direct statement.

astra.reason: The speaker criticizes selling advanced AI chips to China by contrasting the deal with China's cyberattack.
astra.confidence_reason: The speaker's own critical framing supports restricting the sale, although the explicit negative assessment is attributed to experts.

export_controls.text: I don't know how anybody can be okay with this chip sale, given what literally just happened two months ago. And that is something that I think we need to find a way as a Congress to deal with because the administration, I fear, has made a grave mistake.

deepseek.reason: He calls the chip sale a grave mistake and says Congress needs to find a way to deal with it.
deepseek.confidence_reason: The statement clearly opposes the advanced chip sale to China and urges congressional action.

export_controls.text: The Chinese government just launched the first-ever AI-powered cyber attack against our country that we know of. At the same time, President Trump is selling the powerful H200 Nvidia chips, the next generation chips, to China. [...] Why in the world, given that they just did this, what, a couple months ago, would we be giving them these next generation chips now? At the very least, we ought to be holding them back until we have some way of verifying that these chips are not going to be used to attack us.
export_controls.context: House committee hearing on quantum, AI, and cloud cybersecurity, where the congressman presses expert witnesses on the national-security implications of exporting advanced AI chips to China.

deepseek.reason: He calls for holding back H200 chips to China until there is verification they will not be used to attack the US.
deepseek.confidence_reason: The statement explicitly advocates withholding advanced AI chip exports to China pending verification.

We discussed AI, U.S. trade policy, and how Rhode Island can attract investment, grow exports, and stay competitive in the global economy. https://t.co/Dbs25ZzWkR

deepseek.reason: The statement discusses general trade and export growth, not restrictions on overseas access to advanced AI chips.
deepseek.confidence_reason: The text is about a general trade summit and does not mention AI export controls.
